summary: An L-4 cab on a stone rubble base in the Payette National Forest, built around 1932-1933 and still staffed for fire detection as of 2025.

facts.design: Region 1/L-4 cab on a short stone rubble tower

access.note: Drive-up access per Idaho Fire Lookouts, but it is an active, staffed fire lookout and not open for climbing or rental during fire season.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest

events.note: Region 1/L-4 cab built on a stone rubble tower.
An alternate source dates a standard L-4 lookout house to 1933.
Cindi Lee listed as lookout, the most recent name on the historical roster besides the 2025 entry.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on November 29, 2020.
Michael Hass listed as staffing the lookout.

evidence.quote:
Sturgill Peak is a Region1/L-4 cabin design on a short, stone rubble tower.
Built in 1932, it continues to be staffed for fire detection.
1933: A standard L-4 lookout house constructed.

evidence.supports: staffing roster including 1942 Verdie Williams and 2025 Michael Hass
evidence.quote:
1942
Verdie Williams ( Forest Fire Lookout Page )

This L-4 cab, built in 1932, is staffed during the summer. Known lookout personnel: 1942: Verdie Williams; 1944: Bob Donaly; 1952: Don Sewell; 1953: Lane Williams; 1955: Earl Glenn; 1960: Frank Odom; 1960 late season: David Miller; 1961: Larry Daniels; 1962: Melvin Hopkins; 1965: Bruce Feldtman; 1966: Gerald Moore; 1967: Douglas Laird; 1984: Cindi Lee.
Built in 1932, it continues to be staffed for fire detection.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, Idaho Fire Lookouts, and Firelookout.com all give 1932, while an Idaho lookout history page gives 1933 for a 'standard L-4 lookout house.' The story reports 1932 as the main date and notes the one-year discrepancy.

notes_for_editor: Consistent, well-documented staffing history and an active-use status make this one of the more straightforward entries. Only wrinkle is the 1932 vs 1933 build-year discrepancy, noted in the story.
